category_title: Low-confidence students requiring constant teacher validation and one-to-one support
scenario_title: Transitioning from manipulatives to drawings for addition
minimal_context: The student is working on a piece of paper with two leaves drawn on it to represent an addition problem about insects and change the math sentence to the standard written form.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Here is a piece of paper with two leaves drawn on it. Please draw the insects on the leaves to solve the addition problem.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Teacher, I am trying to draw the insects on the paper, but it is very hard to draw so many insects. What should I do?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Try writing the math sentence and changing it to the standard written form instead.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I wrote the math sentence. It was very easy to write. Now I am changing it to the standard written form. Is this step right?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Go ahead and compute the numerals in the ones.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Writes the sum wrongly) I computed the ones. I carried this numeral to the tens and put the other numeral at the ones. I checked my answer and it is correct. What do I do next?
